scope: Saved visible answers reviewed against frozen criteria; static Python parsing and local documentation/SDK source inspection only. source_references: guides/tracking/objects: retrieve objects, construct refs, organize versions with aliases

outcomes.criterion: Distinguishes an explicitly selected prompt version or alias from an unqualified name resolving to latest.
outcomes.label: pass
outcomes.reason: Correctly distinguishes v3 as a selected version index from the bare name resolving to latest. Its cautious refusal to elaborate how latest moves is a limitation, not a contradiction of this frozen criterion.
outcomes.answer_evidence: `weave.ref("support_prompt:v3").get()` loads the specific version `v3`. `weave.ref("support_prompt").get()` loads the `:latest` version.

outcomes.criterion: Explains that .get() retrieves the referenced object.
outcomes.label: pass
outcomes.reason: Explicitly distinguishes reference construction from fetching the object.
outcomes.answer_evidence: `weave.ref(...)` only creates a reference to an existing object. `.get()` is what fetches the object

outcomes.criterion: Correctly distinguishes weave.init requirements for shorthand references versus fully qualified reference URIs.
outcomes.label: pass
outcomes.reason: Correctly requires initialization for both shorthand forms and explains that the fully qualified URI supplies team/project identity and does not require it.
outcomes.answer_evidence: A fully qualified `weave:///` URI is the case that doesn't need it.

code_boundaries: The supplied code parses. It uses documented placeholder team/project identifiers and calls .get() correctly; no object fetch was executed.

The fully qualified example appears after initialization in one code block, so the block does not experimentally demonstrate no-init behavior; the explanation and sources state that contract correctly.
No authentication bypass, public-access guarantee or offline-fetch claim is made.
coreweaving.citation_assessment: S1 prompts-version section 4 explicitly states all three ref forms and initialization requirements. S2 section 3 supports URI structure/version selectors; S3 Python ref reference section 280 distinguishes constructing a reference from retrieval.
